overview: The Supremacy (Mega-class) is a mega-class star dreadnought whose design philosophy reflects the industrial and strategic priorities of First Order (34 ABY–35 ABY). Snoke's Supremacy served as mobile capital, shipyard, and palace spanning kilometers of First Order fleet command. Production estimates place the class at 1 unit, though wartime losses, capture, and black-market duplication make precise fleet registries unreliable.
history:
Engineering teams first finalized the Supremacy (Mega-class) blueprints during the political climate of First Order (34 ABY–35 ABY). The mega-class star dreadnought was intended to solve specific fleet gaps—whether planetary assault, convoy escort, starfighter superiority, or terror bombardment—and shipwrights iterated hull plates, reactor output, and crew compartments accordingly.

Once deployed, the Supremacy (Mega-class) appeared in fleet actions that defined its reputation. Snoke's Supremacy served as mobile capital, shipyard, and palace spanning kilometers of First Order fleet command. Combat logs show crews exploiting the class's strengths while improvising fixes for known weaknesses under fire, a pattern repeated across every major galactic conflict.

As doctrine evolved, rival factions studied captured Supremacy (Mega-class) hulls. Refit yards duplicated weapons mounts and sensor suites; some variants never appeared in official manifests. Estimated production of 1 unit therefore understates how many similar silhouettes operated under alternate insignia.

Surviving Supremacy (Mega-class) vessels now sit in museum orbits, mercenary fleets, and scrap worlds. Historians treat the class as a measure of how galactic wars industrialize violence—each hull a factory product that outlived the politicians who ordered it.
significance:
The Supremacy (Mega-class) demonstrates how mega-class star dreadnought design shapes campaign outcomes. Its layout influenced successor programs and remains a case study in naval academies.

With roughly 1 unit hulls associated with First Order (34 ABY–35 ABY), the class became a visual symbol of its faction's reach—recognizable in holonet footage and feared in convoy manifests.

Engineers still debate whether the Supremacy (Mega-class) prioritized firepower over crew survival; that trade-off defines its legacy in both propaganda and honest after-action reports.
